title: Meet Bills Legend Darryl Talley This Weekend In Hamburg, NY - NewsBreak
text:
By Brett Alan ,
8 hours ago
The World’s Largest Yard Sale is coming this weekend to the Hamburg Fairgrounds and you’ve got a chance to meet one of the former stars from the Buffalo Bills.
Get ready to get your shopping on and meet a Buffalo Bills alumni
What is The World’s Largest Yard Sale? For those who have never been there before, picture The World’s Largest Yard Sale as a huge community yard sale, only bigger. We open this thing up to just about anybody who has something to sell. Whether its just a person who has a lot of stuff that they’re willing to part with, someone who likes doing crafts, someone who has a home-based business, or someone who works in retail. We’ve got them all.
If there’s something you’re looking for, you might just find it at the World’s Largest Yard Sale.
When is the World’s Largest Yard Sale? It’s two full days of shopping starting on Friday morning. It runs from 9 am to 4 pm on both Friday and Saturday.
Meet former Buffalo Bills star Darryl Talley This year, we’re bringing back all-time favorite Buffalo Bills alumni Darryl Talley to meet with our shoppers. He will be at the Yard Sale from noon until 1:30 pm. You’ll have a chance to see him and get one item signed (but it will be strictly one item).
(Buffalo Gift Emporium) Darryl Talley was on the Buffalo Bills for all four of the Super Bowl years and was known to many as Spiderman because of the sleeves he wore under his pads. You’ll find him on Saturday only in the Buffalo Gift Emporium location right inside the Hamburg Fairgrounds.
Click here for more info on the World's Largest Yard Sale
9 Popular Things From The 90's That Are Still In Buffalo Gallery Credit: Brett Alan (Canva) Landline Phones This used to be our connection to everything. It was the end of the world if you were waiting on a call and someone else in your house was already on the phone. You still see these in people's houses and businesses, but most of us use our cell phones for just about everything. (Canva) Paper maps Yes, you can still get them. But how many people even know how to use them? This is something that kind of got phased out with built-in navigation in cars and maps on our phones. But they're still out there. (Canva) Magazine racks So many subscriptions have gone digital that you don't see many of these anymore. You still see them in doctor's offices and other waiting rooms, but a lot of them have done away with magazines too because so many people just use their phones while they're waiting. (Getty/Canva) Posters for our room It's kind of strange to see poster racks in stores now. When we were at a store recently, my kids even asked me what they were. Kids don't put things on their walls like we used to. Whether it was a poster of some heart-throb, our favorite band, or sports team, we covered our walls with them. You didn't even need to paint the walls because you almost never saw what color they were anyway. (Canva) Gumball machines These were at the entrance of every single grocery store back in the day. You could find ones that took pennies, nickels, dimes, and quarters so you'd beg for your mom's change when you went shopping. You still find them, but not nearly as much as you used to. (Canva) Horseshoes (The Game) Yup, horses still wear horseshoes, but when it comes to the game, you see less and less of these. This was the ultimate backyard game growing up in the 80's (other than Jarts) but over the years, they've found safer ways to essentially play the same game. You'll still see some people pull out the stakes every now and again though. (Canva) Cash Cash is king right? Not anymore. You'd be surprised how many people don't even carry any in their purse or wallet anymore. Everything is done on a card. (Canva) Bike Racks These were outside of every single school and a bunch of businesses. When we were kids, our bikes were our main mode of transportation. We would need a place to lock them up when we went into stores. Now, most bikes are used for exercise. So normally people don't need a place to park them other than their garage. (Canva) Shopping malls Sure, we still have them, but they're nothing like they used to be. In the 80's and 90's, they were our social media. This is where we caught up with friends. We didn't always buy things while we were there, but we were there all the time.
